name: The Kepland
description:
By day, a quiet farmland of vills and hamlets. Homesteads nestled into gently rolling hills, brooks babbling peacefully under the shade of willows, small gossip and simple goods traded alongside one another.

But look closely and you'll notice strange details - hedges and walls taller and thicker than peacetime should require, weapons with signs of recent use kept by the door alongside coats and hats, moats and defenses erected around humble cottages. These might seem relics of some bygone time of fear, but their utility becomes obvious when the sun goes down.

The last slanting rays fall upon the Heard Hills, with their imposing, eerie symmetry. As darkness falls they send a mist across the land, cutting each house off from all others and - the folk say - transporting foul spirits across hill and dale to pluck up anyone careless or unfortunate enough to be caught out of doors. If this first harvest of fools is lacking, the spirits become bolder, creeping through any chink in defenses to besiege houses, pounding on doors, scraping claws across windowpanes, and twisting fear into temptation with their comely wailing.

Some Keplanders have accepted the nightly horrors as one might accept the regularity of rainstorms - they are content to carry on their business during the day and leave the night to its strange habits. Others see the rich soil of the Heard Hills and dream of rich fields. Yet others wonder what power might lie in the Hills, and whether that power might be unseated.

hooks.name: The Hoard Of The Ring
hooks.description:
A youth recently found a strange ring of ancient make in the Hollow Hill - an outlying hill that resembles the Heard Hills in their symmetry but which seems devoid of their grim magic. The ring comes alive in moonlight, shining a thin beam of light toward the heart of the Hills. An expedition of brave souls set out to follow the light, but were set upon by a terrible beast - which bore a striking resemblance to the youth who found the ring - and only one of them returned.

Some now call for a better-armed second expedition. Others call for a more thorough investigation of the Hollow Hill to see if more can be learned about this ring, or if some other tool might be found buried there.
hooks.gmNotes:
Should Our Heroes choose to investigate the Hollow Hill, they should find evidence of a great and arcane struggle that occurred there. Some ancient hero managed to banish whatever force was present in this particular hill, but lost their life in the process, leaving behind a magic sword.

Following the ring's light leads Our Heroes toward the heart of the Heard Hills. Along the way, they should encounter at least two things. First, the same terrible beast which accosted the first expedition, which of course is revealed to be the youth, their body corrupted into some grotesque form and their mind twisted to obsessively seek the ring (will this same corruption also take over whichever of Our Heroes, if any, wears the ring now?). Second, the spirit of the ancient hero who cleansed the Hollow Hill. The latter may be simply a vision moving toward the heart of the Hills, or may stop and speak with Our Heroes (or even join them?).

At last, the ring's light should lead to a dark barrow-entrance. Inside should be a series of encounters and puzzles, laid out and apportioned as you choose, culminating in a powerful magical entity: a spirit, warlock, witch or lich. At this point it should be revealed that this entity and the ancient hero were once lovers, who quarreled and were separated. Perhaps the entire darkness laid upon the Heard Hills - the mist, the beasts, the insatiable hunger for violence - was made in anger after their parting. Perhaps there is some other cause. Will the two reconcile, or will they come to blows? Here perhaps the magic sword proves to be the only thing that can break a curse, or a spell, or harm the entity or its defenses.

Bonus points for devising a mechanic that slowly corrupts the ring bearer. Further bonus points for making the corrupted youth just redeemable enough to entice Our Heroes into bringing them along, so that they may (inevitably) prove treacherous.

hooks.name: Gilly Needs Help
hooks.description:
Gilly, stubbornest farmer in the Kepland, set out a year ago to make a new farmstead on the edge of the Heard Hills, far beyond where any others had yet dared. She took her seven reluctant sons with her, as well as several wagonloads of metal poles, sheets, coils and springs - supplies inscrutable to her countrymen. "Bags of barley would serve her better, or a coffin," they said.

As her sons occasionally slip back into Kepton for a pint or three, it is well-known that Gilly has beaten back the night horrors with strange contraptions of her own invention, and that her first year's harvest from the virgin soil was enviable.

But recently one of her sons stumbled out of the night, badly wounded, with a grim tale to tell: his mother's defenses failed at last. Two of his brothers were killed, two others are badly hurt, and Gilly herself was nearly carried off by some foul beast, and now is barely clinging to life. They surely will not survive another attack.
hooks.gmNotes:
The son is a melodramatic coward, but the threat is very much real.

The approach to Gilly's farm should reveal a wide perimeter of outlandish defenses: spidery arms and spinning discs of metal that twirl threateningly, seizing the power of the wind. Perhaps even getting within this perimeter is a first challenge.

Inside, Our Heroes should find Gilly indeed wounded but clinging to life just fine, thank you very much. She is exasperated with her "good-for-nothing" sons, who are making much ado about fairly minor injuries. Gilly herself is dashing about, attempting to repair her defenses while the day lasts. The damage to said defenses should be frightening in scale. Gilly should express surprise at how suddenly the strength of the attacks on her homestead have increased.

Whether Our Heroes help her complete her repairs or not, the night will fall and a fierce attack will begin. What follows should be a test of endurance in combat: wave after wave of horrors and fiends charging out of the mist. Consider devising some sort of mechanic for determining where and when the defenses fail or hold.

In the end, it should come to light that one of Gilly's sons was wandering outside the defenses the day before - avoiding work as usual - and happened to find a half-buried necklace, which he pocketed and brought home. This artifact is of course what has angered the force(s?) of the Heard Hills, and only returning it to them will pacify them.

This adventure dovetails nicely into the adventure of the ring, should that be of interest. If so, consider including any foreshadowing you might find appropriate (a glimpse of the powerful entity, etc.).

hooks.name: Murder Most Fowl
hooks.description: Someone - or something - has been attacking the feathered flocks of the Kepland. Not one of the night beasts, but something that operates in broad daylight. Word has spread that a band of traveling ruffians has been seen on the borders. Perhaps it's they who are responsible?
hooks.gmNotes:
The very moment Our Heroes take an interest in this problem, the locals should become suspicious of them: "As a matter of fact, you lot match the description awfully well!"

The idea here is that the Kepland becomes hostile and every door becomes shut to them, which is of course a problem in a place where remaining outdoors after nightfall is a deadly prospect.

Flight is of course an option, but if Our Heroes aim to absolve themselves, they should be given the opportunity. Perhaps they surprise one of the bird-murderers in the act, or they come upon the scene of the crime shortly after it happens, with a trail leading away from it.

In reality, there are two causes for this trouble. One is - yes - an actual band of ruffians who have been loitering about the borders of this fat little land, stealing chickens and geese when the opportunity presents itself. Perhaps this answer presents itself first and the matter seems resolved quickly. The second cause - and by far the more troubling - is that creatures corrupted by the darkness of the Heard Hills are starved for sustenance. Quite apart from the horror inflicted on the residents of the Kepland, the area's wildlife are suffering greatly, their prey grown scarce and their numbers dwindling. Our heroes should find the den of a wolf or fox or similar creature: a new litter within, the mother wounded, the father infected with corruption and a nightly menace to his own family.

What will Our Heroes choose to do?
